1.name: Shukla Pratipada
1.title: Day 1 of the waxing moon
1.meaning: Its lord is Agni. A Nanda (“delight”) day, one of the weakest of the waxing half.

2.name: Shukla Dwitiya
2.title: Day 2 of the waxing moon
2.meaning: Its lord is Brahma. A Bhadra (“blessed”) day, one of the weakest of the waxing half.

3.name: Shukla Tritiya
3.title: Day 3 of the waxing moon
3.meaning: Its lord is Gauri. A Jaya (“victory”) day, one of the weakest of the waxing half.

4.name: Shukla Chaturthi
4.title: Day 4 of the waxing moon
4.meaning: Its lord is Ganesha. A Rikta (“empty”) day, one of the weakest of the waxing half; avoided for most work and for setting out on a journey; if the act cannot wait, only its first 3 hours (8 ghatikas) are avoided.

5.name: Shukla Panchami
5.title: Day 5 of the waxing moon
5.meaning: Its lord is the Serpent (Sarpa). A Purna (“full”) day, one of the weakest of the waxing half.

6.name: Shukla Shashthi
6.title: Day 6 of the waxing moon
6.meaning: Its lord is Skanda (Kartikeya). A Nanda (“delight”) day, middling of the waxing half; if the act cannot wait, only its first 3½ hours (9 ghatikas) are avoided.

7.name: Shukla Saptami
7.title: Day 7 of the waxing moon
7.meaning: Its lord is Surya, the Sun. A Bhadra (“blessed”) day, middling of the waxing half.

8.name: Shukla Ashtami
8.title: Day 8 of the waxing moon
8.meaning: Its lord is Shiva. A Jaya (“victory”) day, middling of the waxing half; if the act cannot wait, only its first 5½ hours (14 ghatikas) are avoided.

9.name: Shukla Navami
9.title: Day 9 of the waxing moon
9.meaning: Its lord is Durga. A Rikta (“empty”) day, middling of the waxing half; avoided for most work and for setting out on a journey; if the act cannot wait, only its first 10 hours (25 ghatikas) are avoided.

10.name: Shukla Dashami
10.title: Day 10 of the waxing moon
10.meaning: Its lord is Yama. A Purna (“full”) day, middling of the waxing half.

11.name: Shukla Ekadashi
11.title: Day 11 of the waxing moon
11.meaning: Its lords are the Vishvedevas, all the gods. A Nanda (“delight”) day, one of the best of the waxing half; Drik lists the Ekadashi fast on it, dedicated to Vishnu.

12.name: Shukla Dwadashi
12.title: Day 12 of the waxing moon
12.meaning: Its lord is Hari (Vishnu). A Bhadra (“blessed”) day, one of the best of the waxing half; if the act cannot wait, only its first 4 hours (10 ghatikas) are avoided; the Ekadashi fast is broken on it.

13.name: Shukla Trayodashi
13.title: Day 13 of the waxing moon
13.meaning: Its lord is Kama. A Jaya (“victory”) day, one of the best of the waxing half.

14.name: Shukla Chaturdashi
14.title: Day 14 of the waxing moon
14.meaning: Its lord is Shiva. A Rikta (“empty”) day, one of the best of the waxing half; avoided for most work and for setting out on a journey; if the act cannot wait, only its first 2 hours (5 ghatikas) are avoided.

15.name: Purnima
15.title: Full moon
15.meaning: Its lord is Chandra, the Moon. A Purna (“full”) day, one of the best of the waxing half.

16.name: Krishna Pratipada
16.title: Day 1 of the waning moon
16.meaning: Its lord is Agni. A Nanda (“delight”) day, one of the best of the waning half.

17.name: Krishna Dwitiya
17.title: Day 2 of the waning moon
17.meaning: Its lord is Brahma. A Bhadra (“blessed”) day, one of the best of the waning half.

18.name: Krishna Tritiya
18.title: Day 3 of the waning moon
18.meaning: Its lord is Gauri. A Jaya (“victory”) day, one of the best of the waning half.

19.name: Krishna Chaturthi
19.title: Day 4 of the waning moon
19.meaning: Its lord is Ganesha. A Rikta (“empty”) day, one of the best of the waning half; avoided for most work and for setting out on a journey; if the act cannot wait, only its first 3 hours (8 ghatikas) are avoided.

20.name: Krishna Panchami
20.title: Day 5 of the waning moon
20.meaning: Its lord is the Serpent (Sarpa). A Purna (“full”) day, one of the best of the waning half.

21.name: Krishna Shashthi
21.title: Day 6 of the waning moon
21.meaning: Its lord is Skanda (Kartikeya). A Nanda (“delight”) day, middling of the waning half; if the act cannot wait, only its first 3½ hours (9 ghatikas) are avoided.

22.name: Krishna Saptami
22.title: Day 7 of the waning moon
22.meaning: Its lord is Surya, the Sun. A Bhadra (“blessed”) day, middling of the waning half.

23.name: Krishna Ashtami
23.title: Day 8 of the waning moon
23.meaning: Its lord is Shiva. A Jaya (“victory”) day, middling of the waning half; if the act cannot wait, only its first 5½ hours (14 ghatikas) are avoided.

24.name: Krishna Navami
24.title: Day 9 of the waning moon
24.meaning: Its lord is Durga. A Rikta (“empty”) day, middling of the waning half; avoided for most work and for setting out on a journey; if the act cannot wait, only its first 10 hours (25 ghatikas) are avoided.

25.name: Krishna Dashami
25.title: Day 10 of the waning moon
25.meaning: Its lord is Yama. A Purna (“full”) day, middling of the waning half.

26.name: Krishna Ekadashi
26.title: Day 11 of the waning moon
26.meaning: Its lords are the Vishvedevas, all the gods. A Nanda (“delight”) day, one of the weakest of the waning half; Drik lists the Ekadashi fast on it, dedicated to Vishnu.

27.name: Krishna Dwadashi
27.title: Day 12 of the waning moon
27.meaning: Its lord is Hari (Vishnu). A Bhadra (“blessed”) day, one of the weakest of the waning half; if the act cannot wait, only its first 4 hours (10 ghatikas) are avoided; the Ekadashi fast is broken on it.

28.name: Krishna Trayodashi
28.title: Day 13 of the waning moon
28.meaning: Its lord is Kama. A Jaya (“victory”) day, one of the weakest of the waning half.

29.name: Krishna Chaturdashi
29.title: Day 14 of the waning moon
29.meaning: Its lord is Shiva. A Rikta (“empty”) day, one of the weakest of the waning half; avoided for most work and for setting out on a journey; if the act cannot wait, only its first 2 hours (5 ghatikas) are avoided.

30.name: Amavasya
30.title: New moon
30.meaning: Its lords are the Pitris, the ancestors. A Purna (“full”) day, one of the weakest of the waning half; avoided in all auspicious work.

1.name: Ashwini
1.title: Star of the Ashvins
1.meaning: Its deities are the Ashvins, physicians of the gods. A swift star: for trade, learning, ornaments, fine arts, skilled work and journeys.

2.name: Bharani
2.title: Star of Yama
2.meaning: Its deity is Yama, the god of death. A fierce star: the text gives it only harmful acts, such as ruining enemies, deceit and setting fire.

3.name: Krittika
3.title: Star of Agni
3.meaning: Its deity is Agni, the fire. A mixed (tender-sharp) star with mixed results; Muhurta Chintamani gives it fire rites and ordinary work.

4.name: Rohini
4.title: Star of Brahma
4.meaning: Its deity is Brahma, the creator. A fixed star: for coronations, planting trees, founding towns, sowing and other things meant to last.

5.name: Mrigashira
5.title: Star of Soma
5.meaning: Its deity is Soma, the Moon. A tender star: for making friends, union, new clothes and ornaments, auspicious ceremonies and singing.

6.name: Ardra
6.title: Star of Rudra
6.meaning: Its deity is Rudra. A sharp star: the text gives it only harsh acts, such as attacks, imprisonment and separating friends.

7.name: Punarvasu

7.meaning: Its deity is Aditi. A movable star, good for passing things; Muhurta Chintamani gives it riding, gardens and travel.

8.name: Pushya
8.title: Star of Brihaspati
8.meaning: Its deity is Brihaspati (Jupiter). A swift star: for trade, learning, ornaments, fine arts, skilled work and journeys; Raman calls it the most favourable star, for every purpose but marriage.
8.source: Brihat Samhita 98.4–11; Muhurta Chintamani 2.2–8; Raman, Muhurtha, p. 26–27

1.name: Bava
1.title: Good works
1.meaning: Its lord is Indra. For auspicious things, both passing and lasting.

2.name: Balava
2.title: Rites and merit
2.meaning: Its lord is Brahma. For religious and meritorious acts.

3.name: Kaulava
3.title: Love and friends
3.meaning: Its lord is Mitra. For things based on love, and for choosing friends.

4.name: Taitila
4.title: House and shelter
4.meaning: Its lord is Aryaman. For house matters and finding shelter.

5.name: Garaja
5.title: Fields and seeds
5.meaning: Its lord is the Earth. For tilling land, seeds, house and shelter.

6.name: Vanija
6.title: Trade
6.meaning: Its lord is Sri. For trade, partnerships and long-standing affairs.

7.name: Vishti
7.title: Bhadra, avoided
7.meaning: Its lord is Yama. Nothing done in it turns out well except attacks and harsh acts; it is avoided in all auspicious work.

8.name: Shakuni
8.title: Herbs and spells
8.meaning: Its lord is Kali. Herbs, roots and spells bear fruit in it.

9.name: Chatushpada
9.title: Cows and ancestors
9.meaning: Its lord is the Bull (Vrisha). For matters of cows, Brahmins, ancestors and the state.

10.name: Naga
10.title: Harsh deeds
10.meaning: Its lord is the Serpent. For long-standing works, harsh deeds and taking by force.

11.name: Kimstughna
11.title: Merit and ceremonies
11.meaning: Its lord is the Wind (Maruta). For meritorious deeds, sacrifices and auspicious ceremonies.

0.name: Ravivara
0.title: Sunday — the Sun's day
0.meaning: Ruled by the Sun. Paired with the fixed stars, so its acts are theirs: foundations, coronations, sowing, things meant to last.

1.name: Somavara
1.title: Monday — the Moon's day
1.meaning: Ruled by the Moon. Paired with the movable stars: riding, gardens and travel.

2.name: Mangalavara
2.title: Tuesday — Mars's day
2.meaning: Ruled by Mars. Paired with the fierce stars, whose acts are harmful ones; after midday it is not counted as evil.

3.name: Budhavara
3.title: Wednesday — Mercury's day
3.meaning: Ruled by Mercury. Paired with the mixed stars: fire rites and ordinary work.

4.name: Guruvara
4.title: Thursday — Jupiter's day
4.meaning: Ruled by Jupiter. Paired with the swift stars: trade, union, learning, ornaments, painting and music.

5.name: Shukravara
5.title: Friday — Venus's day
5.meaning: Ruled by Venus. Paired with the tender stars: singing, clothes, play, friendship and ornaments.

6.name: Shanivara
6.title: Saturday — Saturn's day
6.meaning: Ruled by Saturn. Paired with the sharp stars: harsh acts, division, training animals.

restFullMoon.name: Purnima parvan
restFullMoon.title: Full-moon day of restraint
restFullMoon.meaning: On the full-moon day the householder and his wife fast, eating once, and the Veda is not studied.

restNewMoon.name: Amavasya parvan
restNewMoon.title: New-moon days of restraint
restNewMoon.meaning: Veda study stops for two days at the new moon: the new-moon day and the day before. On the new-moon day the householder and his wife fast, eating once.

ekadashi.name: Ekadashi
ekadashi.title: Ekadashi — fast day
ekadashi.meaning: The 11th lunar day of each half of the month. Drik lists it as a fast day dedicated to Vishnu.

uttarayana.name: Uttarayana
uttarayana.title: The Sun's northward half-year
uttarayana.meaning: From the December solstice the Sun’s path climbs north each day, until the June solstice.

dakshinayana.name: Dakshinayana
dakshinayana.title: The Sun's southward half-year
dakshinayana.meaning: From the June solstice the Sun’s path sinks south each day, until the December solstice.

ritu1.name: Vasanta
ritu1.title: Spring
ritu1.meaning: The Sun in Pisces and Aries of the Western zodiac, roughly mid-February to mid-April.

ritu2.name: Grishma
ritu2.title: Summer
ritu2.meaning: The Sun in Taurus and Gemini of the Western zodiac, roughly mid-April to mid-June.

ritu3.name: Varsha
ritu3.title: The rains
ritu3.meaning: The Sun in Cancer and Leo of the Western zodiac, roughly mid-June to mid-August.

ritu4.name: Sharad
ritu4.title: Autumn
ritu4.meaning: The Sun in Virgo and Libra of the Western zodiac, roughly mid-August to mid-October.

ritu5.name: Hemanta
ritu5.title: Early winter
ritu5.meaning: The Sun in Scorpio and Sagittarius of the Western zodiac, roughly mid-October to mid-December.

ritu6.name: Shishira
ritu6.title: Late winter
ritu6.meaning: The Sun in Capricorn and Aquarius of the Western zodiac, roughly mid-December to mid-February.

sheets.tithi: A tithi is a lunar day: the time the Moon takes to pull a little further ahead of the Sun (12°, one thirtieth of a full circle). Because the Moon's pace varies, a lunar day lasts about 19 to 26 hours and can begin at any hour. A lunar month has 30: fifteen while the Moon grows (Shukla) and fifteen while it shrinks (Krishna).
sheets.nakshatra: The band of sky the Moon travels along is divided into 27 equal sections, each named after a star or star group in it. The Moon passes through about one section a day. Each section has a guardian deity and its own meaning.
sheets.yoga: Add up how far the Sun and the Moon have each travelled around the sky, and the total falls into one of 27 equal sections: that section is the yoga. It changes about once a day. Each yoga has its own name. Muhurta Chintamani (1.34–35) avoids nine of them in auspicious work: Vyatipata and Vaidhriti whole, Parigha for its first half, and six others for their first hours.
sheets.karana: A karana is half a lunar day, so each lunar day has two. There are eleven kinds: seven repeat in turn through the month, and four come only around the new moon.
sheets.vara: The weekday. In the traditional calendar it runs from sunrise to sunrise, not from midnight. Each day belongs to one of the seven heavenly lights seen by eye: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn, the same ones behind the names Sunday, Monday and Saturday. That light decides which name the day's Choghadiya (hour by hour) starts with.
sheets.brahma: Brahma Muhurta is the second-last of the night's fifteen equal parts (muhurtas), so it ends one part before sunrise. Its length follows the length of the night.
sheets.abhijit: Abhijit Muhurta, "the victorious hour", is the middle of the day's fifteen equal parts, around local noon, when the Sun stands highest. Its length follows the length of the day. It is not used on Wednesdays, so VedaCal shows none then.
sheets.rahuKaal: Daylight, sunrise to sunset, splits into eight equal parts; Rahu Kaal is one of them, a different one each weekday, so its length follows the length of the day.
sheets.yamaganda: Yamaganda is one of the eight equal parts of daylight, a different one each weekday. It is named after Yama, god of death.
sheets.gulika: Gulika (Gulikai) is one of the eight equal parts of daylight, a different one each weekday, and is linked to Saturn. Drik Panchang and Shubh Panchang list it among the times to avoid, with Rahu Kaal and Yamaganda.
sheets.choghadiya: Choghadiya splits the day (sunrise to sunset) and the night (sunset to the next sunrise) into eight equal parts each, so their length follows the length of the day and of the night, and gives each part one of seven names. Their order depends on the weekday. Drik counts four as good for starting auspicious work (Amrit, Shubh, Labh, Chal) and three as bad (Udveg, Rog, Kaal); Shubh Panchang calls Chal neutral, and so does VedaCal. Drik says it was used for travel above all, and that a good part falling in Rahu Kaal is still avoided. It is a popular practice with no classical source, so VedaCal shows it but does not count it.
sheets.ritu: The Indian year has six seasons (Ritu) of about two months each, set by the Sun: Vasanta, spring (mid-February to mid-April); Grishma, summer (to mid-June); Varsha, the rains (to mid-August); Sharad, autumn (to mid-October); Hemanta, early winter (to mid-December); Shishira, late winter (to mid-February).
sheets.rhythm: The traditional rhythm follows the Moon and the Sun: days of restraint at the new and the full moon, the Ekadashi fast twice a month, six seasons instead of four, and two half-years, as the Sun's path moves north after the December solstice and south after the June one.
sheets.times: All times are for {city} and calculated on your device. Sunrise is when the top edge of the Sun appears, the same rule as Drik Panchang, the most widely used online Hindu calendar. VedaCal's times differ from it by less than 2 minutes.
sheets.about: VedaCal shows the traditional Hindu lunar calendar (Panchang) in plain words. Everything is calculated on your device and nothing is sent anywhere. The guidance describes tradition and is not medical or professional advice. City data © GeoNames, CC BY 4.0.
sheets.masa: A lunar month lasts one cycle of the Moon, about 29.5 days, so it begins on a different Western date each year. A month takes its name from the sign the Sun moves into during it (when the Sun enters Aries, it is Chaitra). The names themselves were given long ago after the star near which the month's full moon falls (Chaitra from Chitra, Kartika from Krittika); today the match is only approximate. VedaCal counts months from full moon to full moon, as in North India; South and West India count from new moon to new moon, so for half of each month the name there is one behind. About every three years an extra month (Adhika) is added so that the calendar keeps pace with the seasons.
sheets.rashi: The Sun and the Moon move through the twelve signs of the zodiac. Vedic astrology ties the signs to the stars, Western astrology to the seasons, and over the centuries the two have drifted about 24°, almost a whole sign, apart. So a Moon in Gemini by the Vedic count is often in Cancer by the Western one. Choose which one VedaCal shows in Settings.
sheets.parana: Ekadashi is a fast kept twice a month and ended the next day. VedaCal shows when to end it: not too early, because the first quarter of the twelfth lunar day (Hari Vasara) still counts as part of the fast, and not too late, while the twelfth lunar day (Dwadashi) is still running. Usually that is the first few hours after sunrise (the first fifth of the daylight). When Hari Vasara runs long, the time moves to the afternoon (the fourth fifth), because tradition avoids midday.
sheets.eclipse: VedaCal shows the part that can be seen from your location: for the Moon, from its first to its last contact with the Earth's shadow, while the Moon is up; for the Sun, from first to last contact, while the Sun is up.
sheets.sankranti: Sankranti is the moment the Sun moves into the next sign of the Vedic zodiac, twelve times a year. Each one opens a solar month.
sheets.pushya: Pushya, "nourishment", is one of the Moon's 27 star sections; Raman calls it the most favourable of them, for every purpose but marriage (Muhurtha, p. 26–27). Guru Pushya is the Moon in Pushya on a Thursday, Ravi Pushya on a Sunday; the times shown are when the two overlap.
sheets.amritSiddhi: Amrit Siddhi, "nectar of success", forms when a weekday meets its own Moon star: Sunday with Hasta, Monday with Mrigashira, Tuesday with Ashwini, Wednesday with Anuradha, Thursday with Pushya, Friday with Revati, Saturday with Rohini. It comes one to three times a month; the times shown are when the two overlap.
sheets.sarvarthaSiddhi: Sarvartha Siddhi, "success in every aim", forms when the weekday and the Moon's star are one of the 34 pairs listed in Muhurta Chintamani (1.28–29). It is common, about ten days a month, so VedaCal does not mark it on the month. The times shown are when the two overlap.
sheets.bhadra: Bhadra is the half lunar day called Vishti, which comes about eight times a month and lasts some twelve hours.
sheets.vyatipata: Vyatipata is one of the 27 yogas, the sum of the Sun's and the Moon's positions, and comes about once a month for about a day.
sheets.vaidhriti: Vaidhriti is the last of the 27 yogas and, like Vyatipata, comes about once a month for about a day.

ui.skyLegendOrbit: Inner ring: the 30 lunar days (Tithi) of 12°, counted from the Sun. The lighter half is waxing, the darker half waning. “New moon” and “full moon” mark where the Moon stands at those moments.
ui.skyLegendStars: Middle ring: the 27 Moon stars (Nakshatra). The one the Moon is in now is highlighted.
ui.skyLegendSigns: Outer ring: the 12 signs (Rashi). Blue is the Moon’s sign, gold the Sun’s.
ui.skyLegendNote: Seen from above, not to scale: only the directions are true. From above, the Moon’s lit half always faces the Sun; from Earth we see part of it, a crescent or a full disc. The Moon and the Sun move counter-clockwise.

ui.installNote: Adds VedaCal to your home screen. It then opens like an app and works without internet.
ui.guideInstallIntro: VedaCal works in the browser, but once installed it opens from its own icon like any app and works without internet.
ui.guideInstallAndroid: Android (Chrome): open Settings in VedaCal and tap “Install app”. No button there? Open Chrome’s menu (three dots, top right) and choose “Add to Home screen”.
ui.guideInstallChrome: If Chrome says VedaCal is already installed when it is not, use the button in Settings: Chrome can mistake it for another app from the same website.
ui.guideInstallIphone: iPhone and iPad (Safari): tap Share (the square with an arrow — at the bottom on iPhone, at the top on iPad), scroll down and choose “Add to Home Screen”.
ui.guideUseDay: Day — the Moon today, the day’s good times and times to avoid, and its facts. The ‹ › arrows change the day; “Today” brings you back.
ui.guideUseTap: Tap any name — the Moon, a time, a fact — to read what it means.
ui.guideUseMonth: Month — the Moon’s shape on every day, days of restraint, fast days and special days. Tap a day to open it.
ui.guideUseSky: Sky — where the Sun, the Moon and the star sectors stand, seen from above. Press play to watch them move.
ui.guideUseSettings: Settings — your city or your location, language, Vedic or Western signs, 12- or 24-hour clock, and theme.
ui.guideOfflineText: After the first visit VedaCal keeps its own copy on the phone, about 2 MB: it opens instantly, calculates without internet and sends nothing anywhere. When a new version is out, it downloads in the background and a bar offers to update. To remove the app, press and hold its icon and choose Uninstall. Your city and settings live only on this phone, so removing the app removes them too.
ui.guideGlossaryIntro: Every name the app uses, in plain words. Open one to read what it means and, where it has them, all its values.
ui.clockAria: Day clock: one turn is one day, 12 at the top
ui.paletteNote: The colour scale is the app's choice, not a rule of the tradition.
ui.clockShowRings: Show what the colour is made of
ui.ringFixed: Thin ring 1 — fixed windows. Red: Rahu Kaal, Yamaganda, junctions, midday and midnight. Green: Abhijit, Brahma Muhurta, Ravi yoga, Siddhi days. Decides.
ui.ringBase: Thin ring 2 — the day itself: weekday, lunar day, star. Grey neutral, orange weak, red avoid. Decides.
ui.ringChoghadiya: Thin ring 3, faded — Choghadiya: popular practice without a classical source. Shown only, does not decide.
ui.needsDirection: depends on the direction — choose it
ui.periodChandra: Moon in the {n}th sign from yours
ui.periodChandrashtama: Chandrashtama: Moon in the 8th sign from yours
ui.birthPrivacy: For your own Tarabala and Chandrabala. Kept only on this phone; nothing is sent anywhere.
ui.birthPlaceNote: The nearest city in the same country is enough: the place only tells which clock the time was read on.
ui.modeGeneralAria: View: general. Enter your birth date to see a personal view.
ui.mineNeedsStar: Your birth data is not saved yet, so nothing personal counts. Finish it in Settings → My data.
ui.birthPickPart: That day the Moon moved into another star. When were you born?
ui.birthNoCity: No such city in the list (it holds cities of 15,000 people or more). Type the nearest bigger city in the same country.
ui.birthNothing: Nothing personal can be computed from this: neither the birth star nor the Moon sign is known.
ui.birthNeedTime: Choose the birth time or tick "I don't know the time".
ui.birthNeedPart: Choose the part of the day or "I don't know".

tradition.brahma: Rising at this time is advised; the commentary adds that "brahma" also means study.
tradition.abhijit: Praised by the learned for all undertakings, except travel to the south.
tradition.rahuKaal: This time is "positively harmful for all good business". Muhurta Chintamani does not name it.
tradition.gulika: The sources disagree: Drik lists it as inauspicious, while Kalaprakasika says that for harvest, trade, repaying debts, medical treatment and study it "has no evil force, it is a benefic". So the app shows it but does not count it.
tradition.bhadra: Avoided in all auspicious work; if the act cannot wait, after midday is acceptable.
tradition.vyatipata: Avoided whole in all auspicious work; if the act cannot wait, after midday is acceptable.
tradition.vaidhriti: Avoided whole in all auspicious work; if the act cannot wait, after midday is acceptable.
tradition.eclipse: The source speaks of the days around an eclipse; avoiding the eclipse itself is a choice of this app.
tradition.pushya: Suited to trade, learning, ornaments, fine arts, medical treatment and journeys.
tradition.amritSiddhi: Drik practice; no classical source found. Every such day is a Sarvartha Siddhi day too.
tradition.sarvarthaSiddhi: "Whatever is done in this yoga succeeds."
tradition.durMuhurtam: Daylight is split into 15 equal parts; on each weekday certain of them are inauspicious.
tradition.noon: In auspicious work 20 palas (8 min) are avoided at midday and at midnight. The 8 minutes of midday sit in the middle of Abhijit.
tradition.midnight: In auspicious work 20 palas (8 min) are avoided at midday and at midnight.
tradition.lagnaGandanta: Rising-sign junctions Karka → Simha, Vrishchika → Dhanu, Meena → Mesha, half a ghatika (12 min) each side. "It gives bad results in auspicious work."
tradition.tithiGandanta: Lunar-day junctions 5 → 6, 10 → 11, 15 → 1, one ghatika (24 min) each side. "It gives bad results in auspicious work."
tradition.nakshatraGandanta: Star junctions Ashlesha → Magha, Jyeshtha → Mula, Revati → Ashwini, two ghatikas (48 min) each side. "It gives bad results in auspicious work."
tradition.pakshaRandhra: Lunar days 4, 6, 8, 9, 12 and 14 are "paksha-randhra". If the act cannot wait, only their start is avoided (8, 9, 14, 25, 10 and 5 ghatikas of 24 min); the rest is good.
tradition.yogaPart: In all auspicious work avoid the first half of Parigha, the first 3 ghatikas of Vishkambha and Vajra, 5 of Shula, 6 of Ganda and Atiganda, 9 of Vyaghata (a ghatika is 24 min).
tradition.bhadraMouth: The first 5 ghatikas (the "mouth") are bad; the commentary: "loss of the work".
tradition.bhadraTail: The last 3 ghatikas (the "tail") are good for all acts; the commentary: "sure victory".
tradition.varjyam: "Poison ghatikas": 4 ghatikas in each lunar star, "very blamed in auspicious work".
tradition.amritKalam: Drik practice: a good window in each lunar star. Not found in the classical sources.
tradition.ravi: The Moon's star is the 4th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 13th or 20th from the Sun's; "destroys all faults". The text does not say which faults; the app lifts those of the day's own elements (a lunar day's or a yoga's first hours, the poison ghatikas, the junctions, a weak day) and not Bhadra, Vyatipata, Vaidhriti, eclipses, Rahu Kaal, Yamaganda or personal faults (a choice of this app).
tradition.eclipseDays: The 3 days before an eclipse are avoided; if the body sets eclipsed, the 3 days before, if it rises eclipsed, the 3 days after; after a total eclipse, 7 more days.
tradition.eclipseStar: The star the eclipse fell in is avoided: 6 months after a total eclipse, 3 after a half one, 1 after a smaller one.
tradition.month_adhika: Not begun now: marriage, building and house rites, vows, the great rites (such as the sacred thread), pilgrimage, travel.
tradition.month_jupiterAsta: Not begun now: marriage, building and house rites, vows, the great rites (such as the sacred thread), pilgrimage, travel.
tradition.month_venusAsta: Not begun now: marriage, building and house rites, vows, the great rites (such as the sacred thread), pilgrimage, travel.
tradition.month_jupiter: Not begun now: marriage, building and house rites, vows, the great rites (such as the sacred thread), pilgrimage, travel. This time is "blamed in all countries".
tradition.month_marriage: Marriage is good with the Sun in Mesha, Vrishabha, Vrishchika, Makara, Kumbha, or Mithuna (only early in Ashadha).
tradition.month_chaturmas: Ear-piercing is not done in Hari-shayana. The app avoids this time for marriage and family rites only (a choice of this app).
tradition.baana_mrityu: Mrityu Baana spoils marriage; it holds at the sandhyas, before sunrise and after sunset.
tradition.baana_agni: Agni Baana spoils roofing a house; it holds all day and night.
tradition.baana_raja: Raja Baana spoils serving a king (official matters); it holds by day.
tradition.baana_chora: Chora Baana spoils travel; it holds at night.
tradition.baana_roga: Roga Baana spoils the sacred thread rite; it holds at night.
tradition.base: The lunar day, the weekday and the Moon's star, each rated for the chosen activity; how they combine is a rule of this app.
tradition.hora: The day is split into 24 horas, each ruled by a planet; the day's first hora belongs to the weekday's lord. An act meant for a weekday may, if it cannot wait, be done in that weekday's planet's hora; so a hora suits the activities its planet's weekday suits (drawn from two rules, not one sentence).
tradition.anandadi: 28 yogas from the weekday and the Moon's star together; "each gives the fruit its name says". Which are good is marked by Drik; the bad ones are a regional custom, so the app does not count them; the first 4 ghatikas of Padma are bad.
tradition.pushkara: Lunar day 2, 7 or 12 on a Sunday, Tuesday or Saturday with certain stars: "death, loss or gain is tripled" (Tri) or doubled (Dwi). So the app counts it neither good nor bad – it only shows it.
tradition.sankranti: 16 ghatikas before the Sun enters Karka, Vrishabha, Simha, Vrishchika, Kumbha; 8 each side of Tula and Mesha; 16 after entering the other signs – "very meritorious" for bathing and gifts. The app counts them good for spiritual rites.
tradition.panchaka: With the Moon in Kumbha or Meena these are not done: cremation, travel south, making a bed, roofing a house, gathering firewood.
tradition.dishaShool: Each weekday has a direction not travelled that day. The directions as Drik gives them: Sunday and Friday west, Monday and Saturday east, Tuesday and Wednesday north, Thursday south.
tradition.dawn: For travel dawn is good, except travel east. The time as Drik draws it (the tenth of the night before sunrise).
tradition.godhuli: For travel the time after sunset is good, except travel west. The time as Drik draws it.
tradition.nishita: For travel the time around midnight is good, except travel north. The time as Drik draws it.
tradition.tara: The Moon's star counted from your birth star, in three cycles of nine. In the first cycle Janma (your own star), Vipat ("danger"), Pratyari ("obstacles") and Vadha ("slaughter") are bad; in the second only one quarter of the 3rd, 5th and 7th, and the 1st; in the third "all are auspicious". The text gives each bad tara a remedy (a gift), so the app marks it "only if it cannot wait", not "avoid". Drik grades the three cycles alike; the app follows the base text.
tradition.chandra: The Moon's sign counted from your birth sign: the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th and 11th are good, the 4th and 12th bad, the 2nd, 5th and 9th bad while the Moon wanes and good while it waxes — the app marks the bad ones "only if it cannot wait". The 8th is Chandrashtama, when "nothing auspicious or important to one's welfare should be started": avoid.
tradition.janma: Your birth lunar day is avoided in all auspicious work. The text names your birth month too, but its marriage chapter narrows that to the marriage of a first-born, so the app shows the birth month and does not count it (a choice of this app).
